answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. The upshot is a network where trust is a resource you earn, not a quantity you can mint — and that is what keeps Sybil attacks economically unviable.. It is effective because voting power is weighted by verifiable work over time, so a fresh flood of accounts cannot manufacture a decisive vote. Consider a summit as the anchor of the cost.
